PullRequest.Title: mcp: Activate lazy providers in Agent Customizations
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #327317

## Problem

Extension-contributed MCP providers are registered as uncached lazy collections with no initial server definitions. Opening **Agent Customizations > MCP Servers** refreshed the already-materialized server list but did not activate those collections, so the provider extension remained inactive and its servers were absent.

Running another discovery command such as **MCP: List Servers** activated the same provider and made the server appear, which explains why reinstalling or interacting with the regular VS Code MCP surface temporarily repaired the Agent Customizations list.

## Change

Activate MCP collections when the MCP management section becomes visible and when MCP access is restored while that section is already visible.

Activation remains scoped to explicit user intent: this does not eagerly activate MCP providers during workbench startup. It is gated by MCP access, repeated visibility notifications remain idempotent, and provider activation failures are surfaced through the notification service.

## Validation

- `npm run gulp compile-client`
- `scripts/test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\aiCustomization\mcpListWidget.test.js` — 43 passing
- Targeted ESLint and `git diff --check`
- Added coverage for:
  - activation on the first visible transition;
  - no activation while MCP access is disabled;
  - activation when access is restored while visible;
  - user-visible activation errors.
- Live Code OSS A/B with an isolated profile and a lazy extension-contributed MCP provider:
  - Unpatched: opening Agent Customizations left the provider inactive and the server absent; running **MCP: List Servers** activated it and made the server appear.
  - Patched: opening the MCP section activated the provider immediately and showed the server before any discovery command was run.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Agent Customizations > MCP Servers for the first time with MCP access enabled and one or more uncached extension-contributed collections
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The section's existing refresh and gallery rendering can proceed immediately; the new activateCollections call is fire-and-forget. Extension-provided rows cannot appear until lazy collection activation and provider registration finish, but activation does not block the initial section render.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Activate each uncached MCP collection's extension activation event and wait for initial provider promises
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One activation-event request per uncached allowed lazy collection; discoverCollections starts all such requests with Promise.all. ExtensionHostManager caches each activation event, and an extension itself is activated at most once even if it contributes multiple collection events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening this section did not request lazy collection activation; another MCP discovery command had to introduce the same IPC later.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the initial UI render path because setVisible does not await activation; it is on the path for extension-provided servers becoming visible.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one cold snapshot request per widget while no snapshot is loaded; loading/failure state suppresses duplicate requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same setVisible refresh already initiated this gallery query before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous and independently populates marketplace entries.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number U of allowed uncached lazy MCP collections after policy filtering; activation fan-out is U, while extension-host managers process the event requests concurrently and cache each event.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: McpRegistry uses Promise.all across U lazy collections. Each activation event fans out across applicable extension-host managers, whose per-event promises are cached. There is no new limiter, but U is the number of installed uncached MCP collection contributions, not the number of servers.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Uncached lazy collections are activated once and then replaced by normal collections or removed; cached lazy collections are excluded. Extension activation events are promise-cached by ExtensionHostManager. The gallery snapshot remains cached in the widget after a successful query.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed setVisible call reaches discoverCollections, its Promise.all fan-out, and extension service activation directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider activation duration and the number of installed uncached provider collections vary by profile; no repository evidence shows a harmful burst for realistic U.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The new boundary work is necessary to materialize the requested list, is gated on explicit visibility and access, runs off the initial render path, and is cached after discovery.

Scenarios.Scenario: Leave and reopen the MCP Servers section after all lazy collections are known
Scenarios.CriticalPath: setVisible schedules activateCollections and refresh without awaiting either. discoverCollections resolves without extension activation, then McpService reconciles collected server definitions on a microtask; the initial section display is not blocked by the returned promise.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number S of currently collected MCP server definitions. The existing reconciliation maps S definitions and matches current servers with linear searches, giving O(S^2) comparisons on each false-to-true visibility transition.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One fire-and-forget activation per actual hidden-to-visible transition; duplicate setVisible(true) notifications are suppressed. Reconciliation runs serially on the renderer/main thread after the empty discovery promise resolves.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The extension activation cache and registry lazy state eliminate extension-host IPC on the warm path. The widget does not suppress the service-level warm reconciliation, although unchanged arrays avoid publishing a new server observable value.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the repeated warm reconciliation; low for material user-visible impact at realistic MCP server counts.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repository evidence does not establish realistic server counts large enough for the identifier comparisons and short-lived arrays to cause measurable latency, especially beside the existing list refresh/render.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Although the diff adds repeated warm reconciliation, the available evidence supports only a speculative micro-optimization rather than a concrete performance regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore MCP access while the MCP Servers section is already visible
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The changed activation request is fire-and-forget. Existing code independently starts either the current gallery search or a refresh; provider rows appear after activation publishes server definitions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Activate uncached extension-contributed MCP collections and await provider registration
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per allowed uncached lazy collection, concurrently, with extension-host event promise caching.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Restoring access while visible only refreshed/searched; it did not activate lazy provider extensions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not awaited by updateAccessState, but required before newly activated provider servers can be listed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resume an MCP gallery text query or snapshot query
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One current query; cancellation tokens replace prior gallery work, and snapshot/loading state suppresses duplicates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The access-restoration branch already performed this query or refresh before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronously populates marketplace results and is independent of extension provider activation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Uncached allowed collection count U for activation, plus one current gallery request determined by the existing search state.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Lazy collection loads run with Promise.all; the existing gallery operation runs concurrently rather than serially behind activation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Successful lazy discovery removes the uncached state; extension events are cached. Gallery requests use cancellation and retain successful snapshot data within the widget.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: configuration change reaches the added activation line only when access changes to enabled and the section is visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Rapid disable/enable toggling could overlap registry discovery calls, but extension activation events are coalesced and this is not a realistic high-frequency workflow.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The introduced activation is required by restored access, does not serialize the existing network/UI work, and is effectively one cold activation per provider.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced MCP section visibility and access restoration through registry discovery, extension-host activation, server reconciliation, widget refresh, and gallery queries. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was established.
